newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: Yields ended marginally up because of confusion surrounding a five party deal over new legislation regarding the Riksbank.

Details about the deal, stating that the parties wanted to enhance the credibility for monetary policies through several measures, were published only after market close. However, a statement from the Finance Ministry that an accord had been reached came out shortly beforehand, pushing yields higher.
Yields had fallen during the afternoon because of strength from Spanish markets, but they weakened before closing.
Trade was thin ahead of the end of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, however.
"I think the result of the FOMC meeting will have a big impact on yields for the next month or so," one dealer said.
The crown was unchanged at 4.4740 crowns against the mark but had been stronger earlier on heavy selling of the dollar against various European currencies.
The six month T-bill rate was one basis point higher at 4.20 percent and the ten year bond yield was up two basis points at 6.95 percent.
